## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Wire the sourced-assertion substrate (assertion_store/ + mcp_server/) into one existing workflow so it has a real consumer. This is Phase 1 of the framework memory evolution plan. Recommended consumer: facilitator synthesis at /review close — for each blocking finding, emit a sourced assertion to the substrate cited to the review report file+line range. Phase 0 (SPEC-20260515-053533) committed at a57f3c1 on feature/sourced-assertion-substrate; Phase 1 stacks on top of that commit on the same branch.
- **Files/scope**: .claude/agents/facilitator.md (new emission instruction in synthesis section); .claude/commands/review.md (pointer to the agent step); tests/test_review_substrate_emission.py (new); CLAUDE.md Capture Pipeline section; memory/projects/_self.md (Solution Path [framework/substrate-consumer]); BUILD_STATUS.md. Possibly scripts/emit_assertions_from_review.py (NEW) if R-4 picks the wrapper-script alternative.
- **Developer-stated motivation**: Memory primitives only prove themselves through consumption. The substrate is theoretically validated (Phase 4 canonical test) but has no in-framework consumer. Continuing to Phase 2 (design four more primitives) without exercising the substrate would accumulate untested design assumptions. Phase 0 showed what unconsumed seams look like (5-week silent failure); Phase 1 prevents the analog at the consumer layer.
- **Explicit constraints**: Risk tier medium. Mandatory specialists qa-specialist, architecture-consultant, security-specialist (sanitisation concern: review findings can contain code excerpts with secrets). Per-spec defaults: blocking-only emission (R3), source_ref points at review report not events.jsonl (R2), MCP-fallback to in-process Substrate when MCP unreachable (R6, but spec review should challenge soft-fail vs hard-fail), no schema migration (C2), no backfill (C4), no UI surface (out of scope). Real-world signal: this session's MCP server is registered but its tools are not loaded — substrate IS reachable in-process via Substrate class. Branch: continue on feature/sourced-assertion-substrate stacked on a57f3c1. Phase 0 education-gate deferral logged with trigger 'before merging the Phase 0 + Phase 1 stack to main'.

## QA Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (confidence 0.84)

Three blocking findings (F1, F2, F3) require spec-level resolution before build.

### F1 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — distance threshold mismatch with canonical test
The spec's R7.4 + acceptance criterion uses distance < 1.5 ("moderate band per ADR-0014"). The actual canonical test at tests/test_mcp_server.py:TestRoundtrip uses distance < 2.0 with explicit commentary: "We don't pin an absolute value because the model and corpus state evolve." The spec threshold is stricter than canonical and not justified by any ADR-0014 text. Also, distance thresholds are flaky across corpus growth and model versions.
Recommendation: replace distance < 1.5 with distance < 2.0 AND a rank-based assertion (hits[0]["subject"] == expected_subject). Rank is stable; absolute distance isn't.

### F2 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — synthetic secret fixture design unspecified
The spec mandates a refuse-on-secret test (R7.6, C6) but doesn't specify what "synthetic secret pattern" means. The 12 patterns in validate_tool_use.py:61-93 are specific (e.g., ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}). Constructing a synthetic value that reliably matches without being a real secret requires care. Note: validate_tool_use.py:217 exempts test files from secret scanning, so the fixture CAN be written to tests/, but the design ambiguity will produce either a weak test (string doesn't match any pattern) or a fragile one (realistic token propagates).
Recommendation: spec must specify the fixture value. Use AWS's documented example AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE — matches AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, publicly known, not a real secret.

### F3 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — emit-vs-seal ordering window unresolved
R-3 says emission happens before seal so line numbers are written against the final report state. But R-3 also names a concrete edit that could happen between synthesis and seal: adding the discussion ID to the report frontmatter. The mitigation assumes no edits in the window but doesn't say WHEN the discussion ID is added.
Recommendation: spec must explicitly state either (a) discussion ID added BEFORE emission, so emission sees final layout, or (b) discussion ID added AFTER emission, drift is documented in CLAUDE.md Known Limitations.

### F4 (MEDIUM/ADVISORY) — Substrate-direct fallback tag not asserted in test
R7 asserts assertions land but doesn't assert the "emitted via Substrate-direct" tag was captured. Without this, the swallow-avoidance commitment from R-1 isn't testable in regression. With unittest.mock.patch on the MCP dispatch path, this becomes a 3-line test.
Recommendation: add sub-assertion that fallback path emits the tag.

### F5 (LOW/ADVISORY) — Zero-blocking-findings boundary case untested
R7's fixture has 2 blocking + 1 advisory. No test for 0 blocking + N advisory case (a clean review with only advisory findings should produce zero assertions and no error). One-line parametrized addition.

### F6 (LOW/INFO) — Phase 0 open advisories carry-forward
Per review_gates.md, advisory findings carry forward to next review. The Phase 1 review report should include an "Open Advisories from REV-20260515-221223" section listing arch-F2 (/promote --list-promoted), arch-F3 (canary content-hash), arch-F5 (swallow-and-warn). Process requirement on the review artifact, not on the spec.

### Strengths
- tmp_path + Substrate(db_path=...) isolation pattern correctly adopted from canonical
- Self-awareness about MCP availability (R-1) is right response to empirical evidence
- Blocking-only filter (R3) directly testable
- C2/C3 (no substrate API changes, additive only) are right guardrails
- Test files ARE hook-exempt per validate_tool_use.py:217 — fixture writability is not actually blocked

## Architecture Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (confidence 0.86)

Two blocking findings (arch-B1, arch-B2) require resolution before build.

### arch-B1 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — Hook location should be a wrapper script, not agent instruction
The spec's R5 proposes encoding emission as instructions in .claude/agents/facilitator.md, but the existing pattern for closure-time pipeline steps is unambiguous: extract_findings.py, mine_patterns.py, surface_candidates.py, compute_agent_effectiveness.py, record_yield.py are ALL scripts invoked deterministically by close_discussion.py. Synthesis lives in the agent because synthesis is reasoning; emission of structured records from synthesis output is mechanical and should follow the existing script pattern.

Three consequences of putting it in the agent definition:
1. Untestable — agent-direct emission is integration-only; a wrapper script is unit-testable
2. Coupled to substrate API — every facilitator dispatch (including derived projects that may not have a substrate yet) carries the substrate API in its instructions
3. Reliability risk — agent-driven mechanical steps are subject to instruction drift, partial execution, silent skip — the exact failure modes Phase 0 just fixed

Recommendation: create scripts/emit_assertions_from_review.py invoked by close_discussion.py as a new closure-pipeline step after extract_findings. The facilitator's only responsibility is producing the synthesis report in the expected shape; emission is a downstream consumer of that report. The facilitator agent definition stays clean.

### arch-B2 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — Source-ref durability depends on an unenforced read-only assumption
R-3 claims review reports are sealed read-only after close_discussion.py and that emission happens BEFORE seal. Verification against close_discussion.py:174-179: the chmod only applies to events.jsonl and transcript.md — NOT the review report. Review report immutability is convention, not enforcement. Any post-emission edit (typo, advisory carry-forward, link repair) silently drifts already-emitted source_refs and get_source returns wrong text — violating Suchness preservation, the core ADR-0014 commitment.

Recommendation, pick one:
(1) Extend the seal: close_discussion.py also chmods docs/reviews/REV-*.md for this discussion to read-only after emission completes. Cheapest, aligns with existing pattern.
(2) Content-hash anchoring: store hash of cited byte range; get_source verifies-or-warns. More work; sets a useful pattern for Phase 2+.
(3) Document the limitation explicitly in CLAUDE.md Known Limitations. Weakest; preserves risk.

### arch-A1 (MEDIUM/ADVISORY) — MCP-fallback contract IS ADR-worthy (write ADR-0015)
R6's soft-fail-vs-hard-fail choice is the first formalisation of consumer-side behaviour when MCP transport is unavailable. Howie, Insight Journal, future consumers will all inherit this. ADR-0014 promised transport-agnostic consumption; the contract for HOW consumers express that agnosticism is framework-scoped.

On the substantive call: soft-fail with explicit "via:substrate-direct" tag IS architecturally correct — MCP and Substrate-direct are two transports to the same logical store. Hard-failing conflates transport health with substrate health. This is different from arch-F5 swallow-and-warn (capture failure = end-of-line); MCP-vs-direct is route selection among equivalent endpoints.

Recommendation: write ADR-0015 ("Substrate consumer transport-selection contract"). Two-page ADR. Records (a) prefer MCP when available, (b) fall back to in-process Substrate, (c) route tagged on captured emission event, (d) contract applies framework-wide.

### arch-A2 (LOW/ADVISORY) — Sanitisation is NOT ADR-worthy
The spec's R8 mentions "ADR-0015 here" for sanitisation policy. Wrong — sanitisation is concrete pattern-matching policy, not a cross-project commitment. Document the policy in the Solution Path entry (R8) and CLAUDE.md.
Recommendation: drop the "or ADR-0015" clause for sanitisation from R8.

### arch-A3 (MEDIUM/ADVISORY) — Preregister rough edges as acceptance criterion
The developer's sequencing principle frames Phase 1 as "cure in vivo." A consumer that finds zero rough edges is a failed Phase 1 — it means the consumer is too trivial to exercise the substrate.
Recommendation: add to acceptance criteria: "Phase 1 build summary includes a 'Surfaced Edges' section enumerating at least 3 substrate or consumer-side concerns discovered during build (MCP availability fork, source-ref drift, sanitisation surface gaps, (s,p,o) extraction quality, project_id resolution edge cases). Zero surfaced edges blocks Phase 2 start until investigation explains why." The MCP-unavailability finding already counts as one.

### arch-A4/A5 (INFO) — Boundaries correct
/retro and /deliberate as emission consumers correctly out of scope for Phase 1.
Phase 0 debt (arch-F2, arch-F3, arch-F5) correctly remains Phase 1+ debt.

### Strengths
- Pre-build search (Step 1.5) is thorough
- Real-world MCP signal correctly escalated in Context, not buried
- C2 (no substrate API changes) is right boundary commitment
- Acceptance criterion R7.5 (get_source byte-equal verbatim) correctly tests Suchness, not just retrieval
- Soft-fail-with-tag is the right architectural answer (arch-A1)

### Boundary integrity note
Spec asked whether substrate citing docs/reviews/REV-*.md is a cross-layer leak. NOT a finding — sources are canonical, ADR-0014 explicitly lists docs/ in source_roots. Review reports are sources from the substrate's perspective. This is exactly what the substrate was designed for.

## Security Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (confidence 0.87)

Two blocking findings on R4/C6 sanitisation. Threat surface is narrow (internal tooling, no public exposure) but residual risk is non-zero and persistent — secrets written to SQLite survive sessions.

### Finding 1 (HIGH/BLOCKING) — Sanitisation must happen at assert_fact call site, not via existing hook
OWASP A02 Sensitive Data Exposure.
The PreToolUse hook (validate_tool_use.py) only fires on Write/Edit tool calls — NOT on in-process SQLite writes via assert_fact. The substrate's assert_fact path has no equivalent scan. A finding's object field that quotes code containing a test fixture API key (e.g., sk-ant-api03-... pattern) writes verbatim to data/memory.db. A subsequent search_semantic("API key") retrieves it.

Recommendation: sanitisation must happen at the assert_fact call site in scripts/emit_assertions_from_review.py (per arch-B1 wrapper-script choice). Run the 12-pattern scan over subject, predicate, AND object strings independently. If any match, apply the C6 policy. Do not rely on the PreToolUse hook.

### Finding 2 (MEDIUM/BLOCKING) — Refuse policy is correct, not mask
OWASP A02.
Mask introduces incomplete-redaction failure mode. The 12-pattern regex set was designed for clean source file scanning; in prose contexts (LLM-generated finding text), secrets appear paraphrased, truncated, or split. A pattern like sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9-]{95} matches the full token but a finding might quote "...the key sk-ant-api03-XYZ... (truncated)" — partial match leaves 20 characters of a 95-character token, which for structured token formats (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI) is enough to identify issuer and sometimes account tier.

Hard-line recommendation: refuse. If any of the 12 patterns match in any triple field, skip the assertion entirely and log metadata only (severity, file:line, pattern-class-that-matched — NOT the matched string). The single-user local-tool context does not warrant mask's complexity. Developer can re-emit after scrubbing the review report if the finding is genuinely needed in the substrate.

### Finding 3 (LOW/ADVISORY) — Source-ref containment confirmed
Confirmed: docs/reviews/ IS within docs/ source_root (CLAUDE.md default: sources, discussions, docs, memory, src). Containment-checking uses path prefix — source_ref project://<id>/docs/reviews/REV-*.md#L<a>-L<b> will pass. No gap.
Advisory: confirm prefix matching (not exact match) to avoid future symlink-escape edge case.

### Finding 4 (LOW/ADVISORY) — MCP vs Substrate-direct canonicalisation parity
Per ADR-0014, Substrate.assert_fact internally canonicalises source_ref to enforce project_id boundary. The MCP server's _build_source_uri does additional canonicalisation (path traversal rejection at write time, regression-ledger entry 2026-05-12). I could not confirm from spec alone whether _build_source_uri adds protections absent from Substrate.assert_fact direct path.
Recommendation: read mcp_server/server.py:_build_source_uri before implementing the fallback. If asymmetric, the Substrate-direct path must replicate or call _build_source_uri as utility.

### Finding 5 (LOW/ADVISORY) — Project-id conflation acceptable for Phase 1
A finding about code copied from another repo will be tagged with the running project's project_id. This is consistent with how get_source works. Alternative (embedding origin in source_ref) requires cross-project URI resolution, which ADR-0014 explicitly defers (scope=local only).
Recommendation: document as known limitation in spec Consequences.

### Finding 6 (INFO/CONFIRMATORY) — Log-line leakage boundary
Spec proposes fallback event tag "emitted via Substrate-direct due to MCP unavailability." Metadata only — no finding text. As long as emit_assertions_from_review.py logs only the fallback reason and NOT the assertion triple, no log-line leakage.
Recommendation: spec should make this explicit — fallback event content must be metadata only.

### Worst-case scenario walk-through
/review of auth code runs. Finding identifies hardcoded test token (Authorization: Bearer ghp_xxxx...) in test fixture. Finding's object field: "hardcoded credential 'ghp_xxxx...' at line 47". Phase 1 (without F1+F2) emits the triple to data/memory.db. Later search_semantic("authentication token") returns the assertion. Agent now has token prefix in context window; under adversarial prompt injection, could be directed to act on it. Blast radius: local DB, single-user, no network exposure — but secret persists across sessions and is searchable.

Refuse policy (F2) eliminates this path at negligible cost — one assertion lost, finding still visible in review report.

### Strengths
- Soft-fail / MCP-fallback design is architecturally sound
- Blocking-only filter materially reduces LLM prose entering substrate
- Regression ledger awareness — Phase 1 authors know substrate's vulnerability history
- source_ref → review report (not events.jsonl) is right citation target — versioned documents with stable line numbers

## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Wire the sourced-assertion substrate into one existing workflow (facilitator synthesis at /review close) so it has a real in-framework consumer. Phase 1 of the framework memory evolution plan.
- **Files/scope**: scripts/emit_assertions_from_review.py (NEW per arch-B1), scripts/close_discussion.py (new closure-pipeline step + extended seal per arch-B2), docs/adr/ADR-0015 (NEW per arch-A1), tests/test_review_substrate_emission.py (NEW), CLAUDE.md, memory/projects/_self.md, BUILD_STATUS.md. NOT modifying .claude/agents/facilitator.md.
- **Developer-stated motivation**: Memory primitives only prove themselves through consumption. The substrate has no in-framework consumer. Phase 0 showed what unconsumed seams cost; Phase 1 prevents the analog at the consumer layer.
- **Explicit constraints**: blocking-only emission, source_ref → review report (with extended seal), refuse-on-secret hard line, no substrate API changes, no backfill, no UI.

## Synthesis

Specialist verdicts:
- qa-specialist: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.84) — 3 blocking (F1 distance threshold, F2 fixture design, F3 ordering), 2 advisory, 1 info
- architecture-consultant: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.86) — 2 blocking (B1 wrapper script, B2 source-ref durability), 3 advisory, 2 info
- security-specialist: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.87) — 2 blocking (F1 sanitisation at call site, F2 refuse-not-mask), 3 advisory, 1 info

Total: 7 blocking findings (one — qa-F2/security-F2 about sanitisation policy — is essentially the same call from two angles, so 6 distinct). All addressed in the revised spec.

Verification: arch-B2's claim that close_discussion.py only seals events.jsonl + transcript.md was verified against close_discussion.py:174-179. Confirmed; the review report is not currently sealed.

### Blocking findings — all resolved
1. arch-B1 — Moved emission from agent instruction (.claude/agents/facilitator.md) to wrapper script (scripts/emit_assertions_from_review.py) invoked by close_discussion.py. Matches existing closure-pipeline pattern. R5 + R1 rewritten.
2. arch-B2 — close_discussion.py seal extended to include docs/reviews/REV-*.md. New constraint C7. Resolution of R-3.
3. qa-F1 — Distance threshold relaxed from < 1.5 to < 2.0 (canonical-test parity) AND added rank-based assertion. R7.b rewritten.
4. qa-F2 — Synthetic secret fixture specified: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE (AWS documented example). R7.d rewritten.
5. qa-F3 — Discussion ID written to frontmatter BEFORE emission so emission sees final layout. New R-7 in Risk Assessment.
6. security-F1+F2 — Sanitisation at assert_fact call site in emit_assertions_from_review.py; refuse policy (not mask); metadata-only refusal events. R4 + C6 rewritten.

### Advisories adopted
- arch-A1: ADR-0015 added (substrate consumer transport-selection contract). Soft-fail with explicit route tag confirmed correct.
- arch-A2: Dropped "or ADR-0015 here" clause for sanitisation; it lives in Solution Path + CLAUDE.md instead.
- arch-A3: Added R10 (Surfaced Edges as acceptance criterion; ≥3 entries).
- qa-F4: Added R7.f testing the fallback route:substrate-direct tag.
- qa-F5: Added R7.e for zero-blocking-findings edge.
- qa-F6: Phase 0 advisory carry-forward folded into acceptance criteria.
- security-F4: Added R-8 for MCP-vs-Substrate-direct canonicalisation parity (verify _build_source_uri before implementing).
- security-F5: project_id conflation documented as known limitation in Out of Scope.

### Scope decisions confirmed
- Hook location: wrapper script (not agent instruction). Architectural unanimity (arch-B1 + qa convergence on testability).
- Source-ref durability: extend close_discussion.py seal (option 1 of arch-B2's three). Cheapest, aligns with existing pattern.
- Sanitisation: refuse, not mask. Security unanimity on persistent-leak risk in single-user local-DB context.
- Transport contract: ADR-0015 (new). Soft-fail with route tag. Framework-scoped commitment derived projects inherit.
- /retro and /deliberate emission deferred to future phases; Phase 0 debt (arch-F2/F3/F5) remains Phase 1+ debt.
- No automated MCP-vs-direct A/B test; manual smoke at end of build is appropriate level given MCP availability is itself intermittent.

### Spec status: draft → reviewed
Frontmatter updated. Ready for developer approval. Once approved, /build_module against this spec.
